lemma: For every integer m>=1 and Boolean function f:{0,1}^m->{0,1} with exactly t>=1 accepting inputs, f has a fan-in-2 AND/OR circuit with at most tm-1 gates when input negations are free. If primary-input NOT gates are charged and complemented variables may be shared, it has a circuit with at most tm+m-1 gates. Proof: For each accepting assignment a, form the minterm specifying all m input bits, using m-1 binary AND gates. OR the t minterms using t-1 binary OR gates. The total is t(m-1)+(t-1)=tm-1. Under the charged-negation convention, compute each complemented input once, adding at most m NOT gates. This construction includes m=1 and t=1. Consequently, under the free-negation convention, t<=floor((s+1)/m) implies circuit size at most s; under the charged convention, t<=floor((s-m+1)/m) implies size at most s when s>=m. This is an upper bound for sparse truth tables, not a lower bound for arbitrary circuits.

statement: Cofactor sparsity lemma. Let m>=k>=0, let A be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^m of size t, and let I be any set of k coordinates. For each assignment b in {0,1}^I let A_b={x in A:x|_I=b}. Then some b has |A_b|<=floor(t/2^k). If this cofactor is nonempty, its indicator on the remaining m-k coordinates has a fan-in-2 AND/OR circuit with free input negations of size at most floor(t/2^k)(m-k)-1; if it is empty, its indicator is the constant 0 and needs no gates. Proof: the 2^k fibers A_b partition A, so their integer sizes sum to t; if all exceeded floor(t/2^k), their sum would exceed t. For a nonempty chosen fiber of size u, apply the minterm construction: u minterms each use m-k-1 AND gates and their OR uses u-1 gates, total u(m-k)-1, which is at most floor(t/2^k)(m-k)-1. The empty case is represented by constant 0. This gives a small cofactor only; it does not imply a small circuit for the original function or a gate-elimination lower bound.

proved_step: statement: Cofactor-decomposition upper bound. Let m>=1, 0<=k<=m, and let f:{0,1}^m->{0,1} have nonempty support A of size t. Fix any set I of k input coordinates, and let q be the number of assignments b in {0,1}^I for which the fiber A_b={x in A:x|_I=b} is nonempty. In the fan-in-2 AND/OR basis with free input negations and constants available, f has a circuit with at most t(m-k)+qk-1 gates. Proof: For each nonempty fiber b, form its selector conjunction on I, using k-1 AND gates when k>=1 (for k=0 the selector is the constant 1 and costs zero). On the remaining m-k variables, write the fiber indicator as the OR of its u_b minterms, where u_b=|A_b|; this takes u_b(m-k)-1 gates when m-k>=1. If m-k=0, each nonempty residual fiber is the constant 1 and takes zero gates; the same expression u_b(m-k)-1 is then not used as a literal gate count. Combine selector and residual indicator with one AND gate when both are nonconstant; if either is constant 1, omit that gate, and if the selector is constant 1 use the residual indicator directly. Finally OR the q resulting fiber terms with q-1 gates. For k,m-k>=1 the total is sum_b[u_b(m-k)-1]+q(k-1)+q+(q-1)=t(m-k)+qk-1. If k=0, q=1 and the ordinary support DNF uses tm-1 gates, agreeing with the bound. If k=m, each fiber is a singleton selector and their OR costs q(m-1)+(q-1)=qm-1, also agreeing with the bound. Thus the bound holds in all boundary cases. This is an explicit upper bound for a selected decomposition, not a lower bound for general circuits or a gate-elimination result.

Then: (1) f is a YES instance for MCSP[m^c] under the free-negation DNF upper bound (circuit size <= t*m - 1 <= m^c - 1). (2) There exists a zero-restriction x_i = 0 such that the restricted function f' on m-1 variables has support t (i.e., no accepting input had x_i = 1) and is a YES instance for MCSP[(m-1)^c] (circuit size <= t*(m-1) - 1 <= m^(c-1)*(m-1) - 1 <= (m-1)^c - 1 for all m >= 3). (3) Consequently, for c >= 2, the set of YES instances with support <= m^(c-1) contains functions that survive zero-restrictions as YES instances, so zero-restriction gate elimination cannot force gate consumption on this subclass. Proof: (1) DNF construction: each of t minterms uses m-1 AND gates, combined with t-1 OR gates, total t*m - 1 <= m^(c-1)*m - 1 = m^c - 1 <= s. (2) Since t <= m^(c-1) < 2^m/2 for m >= 3, by averaging there exists a variable x_i such that at most t/2 accepting inputs have x_i = 1. Setting x_i = 0 leaves at least t/2 >= 1 accepting inputs, so support is preserved (not reduced to 0). The restricted function has support t' <= t on m-1 variables, DNF size <= t*(m-1) - 1 <= m^(c-1)*(m-1) - 1. For c >= 2 and m >= 3, m^(c-1)*(m-1) = m^c - m^(c-1) <= m^c - m <= (m-1)^c (since (m-1)^c = m^c - c*m^(c-1) + ... >= m^c - c*m^(c-1) >= m^c - m for c >= 2, m >= 3). Thus t*(m-1) - 1 <= (m-1)^c - 1, so f' is a YES instance for MCSP[(m-1)^c]. (3) Follows directly. This obstruction does not apply to c=1 (linear threshold s=m), where only t=1 survives and the constant-1 function has circuit size 0.

proof: Partition the 1-inputs of f by their assignments to any fixed set of k coordinates. statement: Adaptive cofactor support lemma. Let A be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^m with |A|=t. For every coordinate i, the two cofactor supports partition A, so one choice b in {0,1} retains at least ceil(t/2) points. proof: For each coordinate i, define A_b={x in A:x_i=b}. The sets A_0 and A_1 are disjoint and have union A, hence |A_0|+|A_1|=t and max(|A_0|,|A_1|)≥ceil(t/2). statement: For every integer m>=1 and every Boolean function f:{0,1}^m->{0,1} with support A of size t>=1, there is a DNF circuit over binary AND/OR gates with free input negations, and with no zero fan-in gates, that computes f using at most tm-1 gates. With input negations charged as NOT gates, the same construction uses at most tm+m-1 gates.
proof: For each a=(a_1,...,a_m) in A, form its minterm M_a as the conjunction of the m literals x_i when a_i=1 and ¬x_i when a_i=0. A binary conjunction of m literals uses m-1 AND gates. OR the t minterms with a binary tree, using t-1 OR gates. The resulting DNF is true exactly on A. Total binary AND/OR gates are t(m-1)+(t-1)=tm-1. If NOT gates are charged, create at most one NOT gate for each input variable, share it across all minterms, and add at most m gates; total at most tm+m-1. The cases m=1 or t=1 are included by the same count, with zero gates for one-literal conjunctions or one-term disjunctions.

statement: Restriction DNF upper bound. Let f:{0,1}^m->{0,1} have support A, and fix k distinct input coordinates to Boolean values, where 0<=k<m. Proof: For each of the u accepting assignments to the remaining coordinates, form its minterm, a conjunction of m-k literals, using m-k-1 binary AND gates. Combine these u minterms by a binary OR tree using u-1 gates. The total is u(m-k-1)+(u-1)=u(m-k)-1. Each minterm is true on exactly its designated assignment, so the disjunction computes f'.

statement_start: REPAIRED D2 OBSTRUCTION THEOREM (Corrected Cofactor Support Bound for MCSP[m^c]): For MCSP[m^c] with integer c >= 2 and threshold s = m^c over the full fan-in-2 basis B2 (AND, OR, NOT), let f: {0,1}^m -> {0,1} have support t >= 1. Then:
proof: Proof. B2 model: each gate (AND, OR, NOT) costs 1, fan-in 2, input negations free.

1. DNF upper bound for f: f has at most t minterms, each of m literals, combined with t-1 OR gates. Total gates <= t*m - 1. If t <= floor((m^c + 1)/m), then t*m - 1 <= m^c, so f is a YES instance for MCSP[m^c]. This bound is tight for the free-negation convention.

2. Cofactor support bound (exact): For any coordinate i in [m], let t_0 = support(f|x_i=0) and t_1 = support(f|x_i=1). Then t_0 + t_1 = t. Hence max(t_0, t_1) >= ceil(t/2). At least one cofactor (zero or one) has support at least ceil(t/2).
   - This is tight: for the weight-1 function on m=3 (support {(1,0,0),(0,1,0),(0,0,1)}), every zero-cofactor has support 2 = ceil(3/2), every one-cofactor has support 1. No cofactor preserves the full support t=3.
   - The original S0023 claim "exists zero-restriction with support t" is FALSE; the correct guarantee is only ceil(t/2).

3. Threshold comparison for restricted function: Suppose t <= m^(c-1) so f is YES for MCSP[m^c]. Take a coordinate i where the larger cofactor has support t' >= ceil(t/2). The restricted function f' on m-1 variables has DNF size <= t'*(m-1) - 1.
   We need t'*(m-1) - 1 <= (m-1)^c for f' to be YES for MCSP[(m-1)^c].
   Since t' <= t <= m^(c-1), the worst case is t' = m^(c-1). Then t'*(m-1) = m^(c-1)*(m-1) = m^c - m^(c-1).
   Compare to (m-1)^c = m^c - c*m^(c-1) + O(m^(c-2)).
   For c >= 2 and sufficiently large m: m^c - m^(c-1) > m^c - c*m^(c-1), so the DNF bound EXCEEDS the MCSP[(m-1)^c] threshold.
   Thus the restricted function is NOT guaranteed to be YES for MCSP[(m-1)^c].

4. Obstruction conclusion: The small-support subclass (t <= m^(c-1)) does NOT provide a clean zero-restriction obstruction because:
   (a) Zero-cofactors need not preserve support (only ceil(t/2) is guaranteed for some cofactor, not necessarily the zero one).
   (b) Even when a large cofactor exists, the threshold (m-1)^c shrinks faster than the DNF bound, so the restricted function may become NO for the smaller threshold.
   (c) The weight-(c-1) function W_{m,c-1} (S0052) survives ALL zero-restrictions as YES, but this is a special symmetric function, not the general small-support class.

5. What this means for gate elimination: A zero-restriction gate elimination argument that requires (i) a zero-restriction preserving the MCSP answer and (ii) consuming at least one gate per step, cannot be applied uniformly to the small-support subclass. The weight-(c-1) obstruction (S0052) shows an even stronger survival: a specific function where EVERY zero-restriction remains YES, so no gate can be forced out via zero-restrictions alone.

statement: ITERATED NONEMPTY COFACTOR LEMMA: Let m>=1, 0<=r<=m, and f:{0,1}^m->{0,1} have support size t>=1. There is a restriction fixing r distinct coordinates whose remaining function has nonempty support of size at most max(1,floor(t/2^r)). Proof: Start with the full support. If its current size is 1, fix any remaining coordinate to the value of that support point; this preserves support size 1. If its size is at least 2, choose two support points and a coordinate on which they differ. The two nonempty cofactors partition the current support, so the smaller has size at most floor(t_current/2); fix that coordinate to its bit. Repeat until r coordinates are fixed. While the support size is at least 2, each step at least halves it. Once it reaches 1, the subsequent steps preserve size 1. Thus after r steps the size is at most max(1,floor(t/2^r)), and is always nonzero. In particular, if t<=2^r(m-r)^(c-1), then the resulting function on m-r variables has support at most (m-r)^(c-1) whenever m-r>=1 and c>=2; its free-negation fan-in-2 DNF has at most (m-r)^c-1 gates.

statement: RESTRICTION MONOTONICITY FOR FAN-IN-TWO CIRCUITS: Let C be a Boolean circuit with input variables x_1,...,x_m, gates AND, OR, NOT, and constants, fan-in at most two, unrestricted fan-out, and g gates. No gate is added or duplicated; the graph still has g gates. If the model disallows constants, simplify constant-input gates recursively: AND/OR with a constant either becomes a constant or the other input, NOT of a constant becomes a constant, and duplicate inputs can be wired through. These rewrites remove gates and never increase their number. Thus every cofactor of a size-g circuit has size at most g. Consequently, if f is a YES instance of MCSP[m^c] in this circuit model, then every restriction of f is a YES instance at its reduced input arity with the same threshold m^c (and hence also with any larger threshold). statement: Distance-profile cofactor lemma. Let m>=0, 0<=k<=m, and let A be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^m. Fix a in A. For each b in A\{a}, let d(a,b) be their Hamming distance. statement: For every integer m>=0, every nonempty A subseteq {0,1}^m of size t, and every k with 0<=k<=m, there is a restriction fixing k distinct coordinates whose remaining support A_k is nonempty and has size at most max(1,floor(t/2^k)). If q=m-k>=1 and r=|A_k|, the restricted function has a free-negation fan-in-two AND/OR DNF of at most rq-1 gates.
proof: Induct on k. At k=0, A_0=A, with size t<=max(1,t). Suppose k<m and a nonempty support B of size r remains after k restrictions. If r=1, choose any remaining coordinate and fix it to the unique point's bit; support remains a singleton. If r>=2, some remaining coordinate varies on B, since otherwise all points agree in every coordinate and B would be a singleton. Its two cofactor supports have positive integer sizes u,v with u+v=r. Fix the coordinate to the side of smaller support; the new size is min(u,v)<=floor(r/2). If r<=max(1,floor(t/2^k)), then for r>=2 this is at most floor(t/2^(k+1)); for r=1 the new size 1 is at most max(1,floor(t/2^(k+1))). Thus the bound holds inductively. For the DNF, write each of the r support points as a minterm on q variables, using q-1 binary AND gates per minterm, then join the r minterms with r-1 binary OR gates. The total is r(q-1)+(r-1)=rq-1, also valid for q=1.
scope: Combinatorial support restriction and explicit DNF upper bound with free input negations and fan-in-two AND/OR gates; no claim about arbitrary circuit gate consumption or P versus NP.

statement: For integers m>=1, c>=2, and 0<=k<m, let q=m-k. For every nonempty A subseteq {0,1}^m with |A|<=2^k q^(c-1), there is a restriction fixing k distinct coordinates whose residual support A' is nonempty and satisfies |A'|<=q^(c-1). Consequently the restricted Boolean function has a free-negation fan-in-two AND/OR DNF of at most q^c-1 gates.
proof: Apply the iterated cofactor lemma S0098: there is a nonempty residual support with size at most max(1,floor(|A|/2^k)). Since |A|<=2^k q^(c-1), this is at most q^(c-1), which is at least 1. The residual function has q variables and r=|A'| support points. For each point use its q-literal minterm, requiring q-1 binary AND gates; combine the r minterms with r-1 binary OR gates. The total is r(q-1)+(r-1)=rq-1<=q^(c-1)q-1=q^c-1. This proves the asserted adaptive restriction and residual DNF bound.
scope: A support-based statement about an adaptively chosen restriction and a DNF representation of the residual function. It does not imply that a given arbitrary fan-in-two circuit loses gates, nor that the original MCSP instance is a YES instance.

statement: For integers m>=1 and 0<=k<m, let q=m-k and let A be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^m of size t. There exists a restriction fixing exactly k distinct coordinates, chosen adaptively, whose residual support A' is nonempty and has size at most max(1, floor(t/2^k)). Thus if t<=2^k q^(c-1) for an integer c>=2, the residual function has a free-negation fan-in-two AND/OR DNF with at most q^c-1 gates.
proof: Construct restrictions one coordinate at a time. Suppose j coordinates have been fixed and the current residual support B is nonempty of size r. If r=1, fix any remaining coordinate to the unique point's value; the support remains size 1. If r>=2, the points cannot agree on every remaining coordinate, so choose a varying coordinate. Its two cofactor supports have positive sizes u,v with u+v=r. Fix that coordinate to the smaller side, leaving min(u,v)<=floor(r/2) points. Inductively, after j restrictions the support size is at most max(1,floor(t/2^j)): when r>=2 the next size is at most floor(r/2); when r=1 the next size remains 1, which is the max-with-one bound. At j=k this proves the restriction claim. If t<=2^k q^(c-1), then max(1,floor(t/2^k))<=q^(c-1). Write each of the r remaining accepting assignments as a q-literal minterm, using q-1 binary AND gates each, and combine the minterms with r-1 binary OR gates. The total is r(q-1)+(r-1)=rq-1<=q^c-1.
scope: Constructive adaptive-support restriction and residual DNF bound only; it does not imply gate reduction in the original arbitrary fan-in-two circuit or a guarantee for a prescribed restriction.

evidence: Verified the combinatorial argument: for |A|<=2(m-1)^(c-1), if |A|=1 the claim holds trivially; if |A|>=2, some coordinate varies (else all points identical), its two cofactors have sizes u,v>0 with u+v=|A|, so min(u,v)<=floor(|A|/2)<=(m-1)^(c-1). DNF gate count: r minterms on q=m-1 variables, each minterm uses q-1 binary AND gates, joined by r-1 binary OR gates, total r(q-1)+(r-1)=rq-1 <= (m-1)^(c-1)*(m-1)-1 = (m-1)^c-1. The statement is mathematically correct as a fact about supports and free-negation fan-in-2 DNF size. GAP: The scope note correctly states this does not imply gate consumption for arbitrary B2 circuits - it only gives a DNF upper bound for the restricted function, not a lower bound on arbitrary circuit complexity or a gate elimination step for MCSP[m^c].

Mathematical verification: The inductive construction is correct. For any nonempty A ⊆ {0,1}^m of size t, at each step if |B|≥2 there exists a varying coordinate (otherwise all points identical, contradicting |B|≥2). Its cofactors have sizes u,v with u+v=|B|, so min(u,v) ≤ floor(|B|/2). The base r=1 case preserves size 1. The DNF bound r(q-1)+(r-1)=rq-1 for fan-in-2 AND/OR with free negations is correct. No counterexample exists for the combinatorial statement as given. However, the gap for gate elimination: this proves an EXISTENTIAL upper bound on the restricted function's DNF complexity, not that an arbitrary B2 circuit computing the original function loses gates under the restriction. The restriction is chosen adaptively based on the entire support A, not generically for a circuit.

Mathematical verification: Directly follows from S0098. Since |A| ≤ 2^k q^(c-1), max(1, floor(|A|/2^k)) ≤ max(1, q^(c-1)) = q^(c-1) (as q≥1, c≥2). The DNF bound rq-1 ≤ q^(c-1)q-1 = q^c-1 is correct. Same gap as S0098: this is an existential DNF upper bound for the restricted function, not a gate consumption lemma for arbitrary B2 circuits. The restriction depends on the support A, not on a circuit structure.

Mathematical verification: Restates S0098 with the constructive adaptive proof spelled out. The induction is sound. The DNF bound follows identically. Same scope limitation: proves existence of a support-shrinking restriction and a small DNF for the restricted function, but does not show that an arbitrary fan-in-2 circuit computing the original function must lose gates. The adaptive choice depends on the full support A, not on a given circuit.

statement: For integers m>=2 and c>=2, put B=(m-1)^(c-1). If A is a nonempty subset of {0,1}^m with t=|A|<=2B+1, then some one-coordinate restriction of A is nonempty with size at most B. For t=1, fix any coordinate to the unique point's bit; for t>=2, if A varies on coordinate i, the two fibers have positive integer sizes u,v summing to t, and the smaller is floor(t/2)<=B. Every support of size r>=1 on q=m-1 variables has a free-negation fan-in-2 DNF of size rq-1, so this cofactor is computable by a circuit of size at most B(m-1)-1=(m-1)^c-1.
proof: Let B=(m-1)^(c-1). If t=1, restricting any coordinate to the value of the sole point preserves a singleton, whose DNF uses (m-1)-1 gates (or zero when m-1=1), at most B(m-1)-1. If t>=2, A cannot be constant on every coordinate, since that would make A a singleton. Choose a coordinate i on which A varies. Its two fibers are nonempty and have sizes u,v>=1 with u+v=t. The smaller has size floor(t/2)<=B because t<=2B+1. Restrict to that fiber. For any support of r points on q=m-1 Boolean variables, construct one conjunction minterm per point using q-1 binary AND gates and combine the r terms using r-1 binary OR gates; total r(q-1)+(r-1)=rq-1 gates, with input negations free. Since r<=B, this is at most Bq-1=(m-1)^c-1.

statement: For every m>=0, every nonempty A subset of {0,1}^m of size t, and every integer k with 0<=k<=m, there is a restriction fixing at most k distinct coordinates whose nonempty restricted support has size at most max(1,floor(t/2^k)). Moreover, if the restriction leaves q variables and its support has size r>=1, its Boolean function has a fan-in-2 circuit of at most rq-1 gates when input negations are free.
proof: Construct adaptively. Start with A. While fewer than k coordinates have been fixed and the current support has at least two elements, it varies on some unfixed coordinate i; otherwise all remaining coordinates are constant on the current support and there would be only one point. The two fibers on i are nonempty, with sizes u,v summing to the current size R. Keep the smaller fiber, of size floor(R/2), and fix i accordingly. After j such splits the support size is at most floor(t/2^j), by induction using floor(floor(x)/2)=floor(x/2) for integer x. If the process stops before k splits, the support is a singleton, so its size 1 is at most max(1,floor(t/2^k)); if k splits occur, it is at most floor(t/2^k). For the circuit bound, represent each of the r satisfying assignments on q variables by a minterm using q-1 binary AND gates, then OR the r minterms using r-1 gates. The total is r(q-1)+(r-1)=rq-1. Boundary q=0 has r=1 and the constant function needs zero gates, matching the formula.
closes: D3-D5 restriction-invariant obligation is narrowed to support shrinkage; this does not close hardness preservation or gate consumption.

statement: For every q>=0 and every nonempty support A subseteq {0,1}^q of size r, its Boolean indicator has a fan-in-2 circuit with free input negations using 0 gates if q=0, and at most rq-1 gates if q>=1.
proof: If q=0, the only nonempty support is the unique empty string and its indicator is constant 1, requiring zero gates. Suppose q>=1. For each of the r satisfying assignments, form its minterm using one literal per variable; combine q literals by q-1 binary AND gates. OR the r minterms using r-1 binary OR gates (for r=1, no OR gates). The total is r(q-1)+(r-1)=rq-1. This is nonnegative for q>=1 and proves the bound.

statement: For every integer m>=1 and every set A subseteq {0,1}^m with |A|=t>=2, some coordinate i and bit b have a nonempty fiber A_{i=b} of size r with 1<=r<=floor(t/2). As a support on the remaining q=m-1 coordinates, this fiber has a free-input-negation fan-in-2 Boolean circuit of at most rq-1 gates if q>=1, and zero gates if q=0.
proof: Because t>=2, A is not a singleton, so some coordinate i takes both values on A. The two fibers have positive sizes u,v with u+v=t. Choose b for the smaller fiber; then r=min(u,v) satisfies 1<=r<=floor(t/2). The fiber is a set of r points on q=m-1 coordinates. For q>=1, OR its r distinct minterms: each minterm takes q-1 binary AND gates, and the OR takes r-1 binary OR gates, totaling r(q-1)+(r-1)=rq-1. For q=0, m=1 and the fiber is the sole point of the zero-dimensional domain, whose indicator is constant 1 and requires zero gates.
